Definition: fat, i.e. (literally and abstractly) fatness; but usually (figuratively and concretely) a rich dish, a fertile field, a robust man
BiblicalUsage: mashmân is fatness, the rich part of the land and of life. In Genesis 27:28 Isaac blesses Jacob with the dew of heaven and the fatness of the earth, and in Genesis 27:39 Esau's dwelling is also the fatness of the earth. In Isaiah 10:16 God sends leanness among the fat ones of Assyria, and in Daniel 11:24 a king enters the fattest places of the province and scatters prey and spoil. The word is plenty that can be given or taken.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mashmân shows me that God gives fatness to His people and leanness to the proud. I hold that the fatness of the earth is His gift, not my right.
